- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >70); apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×current sentiment-weighted average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 18-day moving average as baseline for correction if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 15–20% for next 7 days.
